name: mount_setattr
synopsis: int syscall(SYS_mount_setattr, int dirfd, const char *pathname, unsigned int flags, struct mount_attr *attr, size_t size);
Note: glibc provides no wrapper for mount_setattr(), necessitating the use of syscall(2).
description: The mount_setattr() system call changes the mount properties of a mount or an entire mount tree. It uses flags to alter pathname resolution and a structure to set or clear specific attributes such as read-only status or propagation type.

parameters.name: dirfd
parameters.description: Directory file descriptor for relative pathnames, or AT_FDCWD for current working directory.

parameters.name: pathname
parameters.description: Pathname of the mount point; if empty and AT_EMPTY_PATH is set, operates on dirfd directly.

parameters.name: flags
parameters.description: Flags to modify pathname resolution, such as AT_EMPTY_PATH, AT_RECURSIVE, AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW, or AT_NO_AUTOMOUNT.

parameters.name: attr
parameters.description: Pointer to a structure containing attributes to set, clear, propagation type, and user namespace file descriptor.

parameters.name: size
parameters.description: Size of the struct mount_attr structure, typically sizeof(struct mount_attr), to handle extensibility.

return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error, and errno is set to indicate the cause

errors.description: pathname is relative but dirfd is neither AT_FDCWD nor a valid file descriptor.
userns_fd is not a valid file descriptor.

The pathname specified via the dirfd and pathname arguments to mount_setattr() isn’t a mount point.

MOUNT_ATTR_IDMAP was specified in attr_clr.
